Here in Dodoma the rains are not reliable and the soils are tired, so I must be careful with my money. I have no schooling and I have never bought fertilizer from the shop — it is expensive and if the rains fail my money is wasted. I keep a few goats and cattle, so I will spread their manure on this plot before planting, and I will save seeds from last year's harvest like my neighbors do. My wife and I will do most of the work with the hand hoe, but I will call some young men from the village to help with weeding when the maize is knee-high.
